newsitem.title: USA: Judge orders liquidation of Stratton Oakmont.
newsitem.headline: Judge orders liquidation of Stratton Oakmont.

text.p: A federal judge ruled Wednesday that Stratton Oakmont Inc., which was expelled from the securities industry in December, will be liquidated and he appointed a trustee to oversee the process.

U.S. District Judge John Sprizzo granted an application by the Securities Investor Protection Corp. to appoint Harvey Miller, a prominent bankruptcy lawyer with New York's Weil, Gotshal & Manges, to liquidate the brokerage firm.
Lake Success, N.Y. based-Stratton Oakmont filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection last week and was seeking to reorganize as a merchant bank.
The firm had sought bankruptcy protection after the NASD decided in December to expel Stratton from the securities industry due to unauthorised trading complaints dating back to December 1993.
Stratton unsuccessfully sought a stay of the NASD's expulsion from the SEC. It has filed an appeal of that order with the commission.
The Securities and Exchange Commission and a number of state securities regulators around the country also have sanctioned Stratton Oakmont.
The Securities Investor Protection Corp. filed a complaint against the firm Monday in Manhattan federal court seeking a trustee to protect Stratton's assets and to liquidate the firm.
It submitted affidavits from both the National Association of Securities Dealers Regulation and the SEC providing evidence of unauthorised trades in customers' accounts.

Barry Goldsmith, the NASD's executive vice president of enforcement, said investors will have a better chance of recouping lost funds through a liquidation rather than if Stratton Oakmont had been allowed to pursue a Chapter 11 reorganization.
